court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Allahabad, Misc. Case No. 01 of 2019
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized on 09.07.2018 but soon strained. Parties entered into a compromise to seek mutual divorce under Section 13B of Hindu Marriage Act. Both parties are living separately since 12.10.2018. Divorce petition filed under section 13B of the Act was rejected by order dated 23.01.2019 by the Court below as premature.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for divorce by mutual consent cannot be filed before the expiration of one year from the date of marriage.
legal_principles.held: Sub-section (1) of Section 13B is an enabling Section for presenting a petition for dissolution of a marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent. One of the grounds provided is that the parties have been living separately for a period of one year or more and have not been able to live together.
use_in: cases involving divorce by mutual consent

legal_principles.principle: A petition for divorce cannot be entertained unless one year has elapsed since the date of marriage, except in cases of exceptional hardship or depravity.
legal_principles.held: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, it shall not be competent for any Court to entertain any petition for dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce, unless at the date of the presentation of the petition one year has elapsed since the date of the marriage:

outcome.final_order: The divorce petition was returned back holding that the period as prescribed under Section 13-B(1) of the Act can not be waived under the proviso to Section 14 of the Act.

keywords: Latin maxim: 'Nemo dat quod non habet'
